basic_information.short_title: Extension of the 2020 and 2021 Special Development Fund
basic_information.official_title: AN ACT EXTENDING THE AVAILABILITY OF 2020 AND 2021 SPECIAL DEVELOPMENT FUND
basic_information.session: First Regular Session, Second Bangsamoro Transition Authority (begun 15 September 2022)
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: Immediately after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Extends the life of the ₱10 billion Special Development Fund appropriated from the 2020 and 2021 budgets, giving until the end of 2023 to commit it and into 2024 to finish paying for the works.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: The fund was about to lapse with projects unfinished. Rather than let ₱10 billion of development money expire, Parliament moved the deadlines.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: Appropriations under the fund stayed releasable and disbursable to 31 December 2023. Infrastructure could be obligated to that date with construction completed, inspected and paid by 30 June 2024; other items by 31 March 2024.
who_will_be_affected: Communities with projects funded from the Special Development Fund
Bangsamoro ministries and offices administering the fund
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: Took effect immediately on publication in early 2023. Its windows were later extended again by BAA 51.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: ₱10 billion of development money did not expire. This gave until end-2023 to commit it and into 2024 to finish paying — and BAA 51 later extended it further.
in_practice: All appropriations under the fund available for release and disbursement until 31 December 2023
Infrastructure capital outlays obligable to 31 December 2023, with construction completed, inspected and paid by 30 June 2024
MOOE and other capital outlay items obligable to 31 December 2023, with delivery, inspection and payment by 31 March 2024
The Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management issues the implementing guidelines

for_specific_groups.Communities awaiting projects: Development works funded from the 2020 and 2021 SDF did not have to be cancelled.
for_specific_groups.Contractors: Deadlines for completion, inspection and payment were pushed into 2024.
for_specific_groups.Anyone tracking the fund: This is the second act in a chain — BAA 51 extends the same money again, to 2024 and beyond.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The Bangsamoro Special Development Fund appropriated from the 2020 and 2021 budgets.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: Historic in itself; the same money was carried further by BAA 51.
what_you_can_do: Read alongside BAA 22, which appropriated the ₱10 billion, and BAA 51, which extended it again
watch_out_for: Unlike the general appropriations extensions, this one carries no Personnel Services exclusion — the Special Development Fund is a development pot, not an operating budget.
No new money is added; only deadlines move.
The extension was itself later extended, which is the pattern to watch across this fund.

key_terms_explained.Special Development Fund: A dedicated development pot for the region, separate from the general operating budget. BAA 22 appropriated ₱10 billion from the 2020 and 2021 budgets.
key_terms_explained.Obligation: Committing money to a contract, as distinct from paying it out.
key_terms_explained.MFBM: The Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Jumada Al-Awwal 28, 1444 / 22 December 2022, approved by the Chief Minister on 12 January 2023.

benefits.headline: ₱10 billion of development money kept alive rather than lapsing.

direct_benefits.benefit: Projects funded from the 2020–2021 Special Development Fund could continue
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Communities and contractors with pending works
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Automatic — it changed deadlines, not processes

indirect_benefits: Avoided cancellation and re-appropriation of a large development programme
limitations: Superseded in part by BAA 51, which extended the same fund further.

for_citizens: None. The act governs government spending deadlines.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.first_stop: Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management (MFBM), authorised to issue the implementing guidelines
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A development project in a municipality funded from the 2020–2021 Special Development Fund was unfinished at the end of 2022. This act let the money stay committed through 2023 and be paid out into 2024.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Amends Section 3 of Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 22, the act appropriating ₱10,000,000,000 from the 2020 and 2021 Special Development Fund. As amended, all appropriations authorised in that act are available for release and disbursement for the purpose specified until 31 December 2023. Infrastructure capital outlays are valid for obligation until 31 December 2023, with completion of construction, inspection and payment no later than 30 June 2024; MOOE and other capital outlay items are likewise obligable until 31 December 2023, with delivery, inspection and payment no later than 31 March 2024. The MFBM is authorised to issue guidelines for the cash budgeting system.
Section 3 — Takes effect immediately after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation.

who_benefits: Communities with Special Development Fund projects
impact.allocated_budget: No new appropriation. It extends the ₱10,000,000,000 appropriated by BAA 22 from the 2020 and 2021 Special Development Fund.
impact.figures_note: The ₱10 billion figure comes from the title of BAA 22 as recited in this act.

citizen_questions.a: The fund it extends is the ₱10 billion appropriated by BAA 22 from the 2020 and 2021 Special Development Fund. This act adds nothing; it moves deadlines.
Release and disbursement to 31 December 2023; infrastructure completed, inspected and paid by 30 June 2024; other items by 31 March 2024.
No. BAA 51 extended the same fund again, to 31 December 2024 for release and obligation — and made it disbursable until fully expended.
